milestone: Brownie MCP Runtime Safety Policy Finite Closure

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Requires MCP tools/call to match task-pinned tool annotation provenance and denies approval-free execution when annotations narrow or contradict structured Brownie safety policy.
Prevents autonomous agent loops from continuing with stale or drifted MCP annotation evidence after tools/list changes.
Keeps MCP execution bounded by task-pinned catalog provenance while preserving Mode Pack structured policy as the authority source.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances runtime_permission_enforcement and headless_autonomous_development while preserving controlled_workspace_tools boundaries.
answers.new_capability: Runtime can parse, pin, fingerprint, and drift-check MCP tool annotations, then use them only to narrow approval-free tools/call execution.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: MCP-S2 added structured Brownie safety policy, but tools/list annotations were still not represented in task-pinned catalog evidence, so annotation changes could not be detected as catalog drift.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A server could change readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, or openWorldHint after task admission without Runtime detecting the provenance drift before tools/call.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase changes MCP catalog admission, task-pinned provenance, drift checks, and Runtime execution narrowing; it does not add a wrapper, adapter manifest, new RPC, or documentation-only verdict.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing tool.execute, task.run, and headless run/resume paths are preserved.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase updates existing policy, Runtime execution evidence, specs, and audits rather than adding a summary endpoint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: MCP tools/call is denied before server execution when live annotations drift from task-pinned catalog evidence or when annotations contradict approval-free read-only safe execution.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Autonomous runs can safely continue using MCP tools only when the live catalog still matches admitted annotation evidence and annotations do not narrow the call out of approval-free safety.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes MCP-S3 and leaves MCP-S4 through MCP-S7 open before Runtime Release Ready.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: MCP-S3 changes Runtime MCP catalog provenance and execution narrowing, so strict review must verify annotations are parsed and drift-checked as task-pinned narrowing-only hints rather than authority.

exit_criteria: MCP tools/list parses bounded boolean readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, and openWorldHint annotations.
MCP catalog entries include annotations and annotation_fingerprint, and task-pinned catalog fingerprints cover annotation values.
MCP tools/call detects annotation drift by comparing live catalog and per-tool annotation fingerprints with task-pinned provenance before server execution.
Invalid known annotation field types fail closed during catalog admission.
Contradictory or open-world annotations narrow approval-free read-only execution before tools/call.
MCP-S3 is marked closed while MCP-S4 through MCP-S7 and Runtime Release Ready remain open.
behavior_evidence: brownie-runtime test coverage proves annotation parsing, task-pinned annotation fingerprints, and annotation drift denial.
brownie-runtime test coverage proves read-only approval-free MCP execution is narrowed by readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=true, idempotentHint=false, and openWorldHint=true before tools/call.
brownie-runtime test coverage proves invalid known annotation field types fail closed at catalog admission.
docs/architecture/mcp-runtime-safety-policy-audit.json records MCP-S3 as closed while leaving MCP-S4 through MCP-S7 open.

accepted_capability: MCP tool annotations are now bounded, task-pinned, fingerprinted catalog provenance.
Annotation drift and narrowing conflicts fail closed before tools/call.
behavior_evidence: Runtime focused MCP test coverage proves annotation provenance, drift detection, invalid annotation rejection, and narrowing-only execution behavior.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains the execution, admission, replay, permission, tool, workspace mutation, and completion authority.
Mode Pack structured policy remains the MCP tool safety authority; MCP annotations, descriptions, schemas, results, and model output cannot grant authority.
Annotations can only narrow approval-free execution or fail closed; mutation and approval-required MCP tools remain fail-closed until MCP-S4 approval binding.
non_goals: Does not add a Brownie-specific tool adapter SDK or protocol.

Does not add Streamable HTTP, OAuth, MCP Apps, Sampling, Roots, Elicitation, public registry, automatic install, scheduler, daemon, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, or recursive Brownie invocation.
Does not close MCP-S4 through MCP-S7.
Does not close full CI workflow hardening while workflow update authority is unavailable.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected treating annotations as authority because MCP annotations are server-supplied hints, not Mode Pack policy.
Rejected inferring annotations from descriptions because prose cannot grant or narrow authority deterministically.
Rejected allowing openWorldHint=true approval-free because open-world effects require later approval binding or fail-closed handling.
technical_debt: MCP-S4 tool-level approval binding remains open.
MCP-S5 runtime input/output schema validation remains open.
MCP-S6 secret reference contract remains open.
Previously recorded Runtime Release Readiness blockers remain open, including full CI workflow hardening.

runtime_release_dod: Runtime-owned MCP permission checks, tool execution, bounded evidence, replay, and completion semantics.
Task-pinned Mode Pack policy, catalog provenance, and point-of-use Runtime safety enforcement.
runtime_boundary_contracts: Existing tool.execute, task.run, and headless run/resume paths.
Existing ToolExecutionCompleted, ToolExecutionFailed, and ToolExecutionDenied ledger evidence.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: Scheduling, background polling, daemonization, hosted queues, worker fleets, and remote server operations.
external_adapter_responsibilities: MCP server implementation, GitHub/GitLab/Slack adapters, OAuth application wiring, and remote transport hosting.
commercial_solution_readiness: Enterprise tenant management, SSO/RBAC server, admin UI, monitoring backend, billing, SLA, private registry, and certified stack.

next_capability_rationale: MCP-S4 should bind approval-required MCP tool calls to one concrete Runtime approval fingerprint using this task-pinned annotation provenance baseline.
